The test `test_pending_fifo` is failing at line 317 with an assertion:
`zassert_false((coop_high_state != FIFO_TEST_START) || (coop_low_state != FIFO_TEST_START) || (task_high_state != FIFO_TEST_START) || (task_low_state != FIFO_TEST_START), NULL);`

This assertion checks that all four threads (`coop_high`, `coop_low`, `task_high`, `task_low`) are currently in the `FIFO_TEST_START` state. This state is set just before they attempt to get data from the FIFO with a timeout. The test expects them to block on the `k_fifo_get` call and not time out yet.

The failure indicates that at least one of the threads has already timed out from its `k_fifo_get` call and incremented its state (e.g., `FIFO_TEST_START + 1`). This means the time elapsed between the threads being unblocked and the assertion being checked is longer than the shortest timeout configured for `k_fifo_get`.

The timeouts are:
- `task_low`: `FOURTH_SECOND` (250 ms)
- `task_high`: `THIRD_SECOND` (333 ms)
- `coop_low`: `HALF_SECOND` (500 ms)
- `coop_high`: `NUM_SECONDS(1)` (1000 ms)

The shortest timeout is 250 ms. It appears that the overhead of scheduling the work item, unblocking the threads, and having them execute up to the `k_fifo_get` call and then timing out, is exceeding 250 ms on the test environment.

To fix this, we need to:
1.  Increase the timeout values for all threads while preserving their relative order. This ensures that the shortest timeout is long enough for the initial setup to complete before any thread times out.
2.  Adjust the `k_sleep` duration in the test functions (`test_pending_fifo` and `test_pending_lifo`) to be longer than the new maximum timeout. This ensures that all threads have enough time to time out for the subsequent assertions that check the order of timeouts.

A `TIMEOUT_FACTOR` of 4 will be applied to all existing timeout definitions. This will make the shortest timeout 1000 ms, which should be sufficient. The `k_sleep` will be increased from 2 seconds to 5 seconds to accommodate the new maximum timeout of 4 seconds.
